correctness.rationale: The conditional Gaussian quadratic-form identity gives twice the expected squared Frobenius norm of the projected residual. For one spike, the projection is a rank-one perturbation of a rank-(d-1) orthoprojector, giving exact chi-square-ratio moments. In dimension four an exact Beta(1/2,3/2) integral gives rational moments and variances; Descartes plus sign brackets prove one positive threshold. For fixed d, Gaussian rescaling and an integrable dominated expansion give the leading linear coefficient with O_d(1) remainder. Standalone code checks 396 identities/numerical cases; those finite tests do not establish the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The published conditional-residual variance identity and qualitative sketch-allocation tradeoff are acknowledged as prior results. The checked primary work does not evaluate the one-spike Gaussian-sketch beta integral, prove the exact three-query d=4 comparison and unique algebraic crossover, or derive the fixed-dimension sharp linear leading coefficient. This is a narrower model-specific quantitative result, not a novel estimator or general query-complexity improvement. An unindexed predecessor remains a risk.

value.rationale: The equal three-matvec constraint makes the deflation-versus-direct-sampling comparison mathematically natural: two sketch-building products are an opportunity cost on flatter spectra. Dimension four is the first setting in which three generic queries are below the dimension, and the exact unique transition is a nontrivial finite-budget tuning boundary. Rare missed-spike sketches create linear rather than bounded asymptotic variance at every fixed dimension, explaining the qualitative mechanism in quantitative form. A complete, exact algorithm-selection benchmark may inform budget allocation and test implementations without claiming a universal estimator.
